read_scope.notes: Read the complete 22-page frozen PDF, including references and Appendices A–G, from extracted text; visually inspected every PDF page, all five figures and all twelve tables. Read paper.tex and specificity_results.tex to resolve terminology, equations, hierarchy and cross-references. Technical appendices were treated as optional depth, not prerequisites for the intended main-text reader. PDF text extraction and page rendering used the isolated /tmp/editorial_r24_c_inspection directory. The abstract contains 152 whitespace-delimited words in the PDF extraction. No other reviews, prior versions, progress records or current non-snapshot manuscript were consulted.

score_reasons.expression: Excellent, precise English with manageable paragraphs and stable definitions of aligned response, total error, calibration and the digital reference target. Section 4.1 explains the scores through actual lightness gaps and the 1/0/1 errors of three idealized generators; Section 5.4 explains why shrinking GPT Image 2 can lower error. Qualifications generally sit beside the claims they constrain. The abstract retains a little compressed technical shorthand, and one results cross-reference is incomplete; these are localized refinements.
score_reasons.structure: The progression from the motivating distinction to reference/design, features, score intuition, estimation and interpretive results is coherent. The first result presents the declared inference, followed by shared response, painter-pair diagnostics, scene/calibration choices and source sensitivity. Sections 4.3–4.4 and the results distinguish declared comparisons from retrospective checks. The main narrative is complete by page 10; derivations, full pair tables, source controls and earlier cohorts are appropriately optional appendix material.
score_reasons.new_reader_understanding: A graduate-level reader can recover the experimental arms, the finite digital target, the role of centering, the meaning of beta and D, and why low error differs from strong response without repository access. Tables 1–5 and the captions explain units, benchmarks, interval scope and calibration. The main text explicitly distinguishes the theoretical D=1 predictor from the generic-painting arm and explains why scene variation is penalized. The abstract could identify the criterion behind “beats” more explicitly, and the all-pairs interval claim should direct readers to the complete table.
score_reasons.engagement: The opening Monet/Sisley example gives the measurement question a concrete purpose. Figure 1 lets readers compare the actual prompt intervention; Figure 2 rewards inspection through common axes and magnified M/S/P details; Figure 3 makes uneven painter distinctions immediately visible. Result headings and the GPT Image 2/FLUX and Nano Banana 2/FLUX reversals sustain a discernible narrative without claiming perceptual success. The abstract compresses several secondary findings into its closing sentences, slightly reducing emphasis on the central alignment-versus-error result.

strengths: Section 4.1, page 5, introduces contrast centering with the observed Monet–Sisley lightness difference before giving notation, then makes the different purposes of beta and D clear with the no-distinction, exact-match and doubled-response examples.

Sections 5.1 and 5.4 connect numerical results to their implications: GPT Image 2 can have near-unit aligned response and substantial total error; Nano Banana 2 and FLUX exchange order when scene variation is included; shrinking contrasts changes calibrated error without changing images.

Figures 1–3 are cleanly rendered and substantively useful. The six-condition image grid, common-scale geometric detail panels and annotated pair heatmaps offer complementary ways to inspect the story.

The source sensitivity is integrated into the main claim rather than hidden: Table 5 and the conclusion show that the Sunburst–FLUX interval becomes unresolved, and Section 5.5 identifies the newly positive GPT Image 1 comparison as retrospective.

The paper consistently bounds its claims to measured digital-reference differences and fixed configurations. It clearly discloses unverified AI source judgments, approximate scene-based inference, and the absence of complete public exact-pixel access.

findings.issue: The abstract says no model “beats” the no-distinction predictor before naming the criterion being compared, while “repeat correction” is also left as shorthand. Its final three result sentences then move quickly through pair alignment, the uncalibrated minimum and calibration. The body explains all of this well, but the standalone abstract asks the reader to infer that beating the predictor means reducing total error, not increasing aligned response.
findings.reader_effect: A new reader may initially find positive alignment and failure to beat a no-distinction predictor contradictory, or may give the model-ordering details as much weight as the primary measurement distinction.
findings.suggested_change: Replace “repeat correction” with “noise correction” and revise the comparison sentence to “All partly align with reference differences, yet none demonstrably beats a predictor making no painter distinctions on total error.” This uses two more words than the current sentence, keeping the extracted abstract at approximately 154 words. If further tightening is desired, combine the two model-minimum statements while retaining the fact that calibration changes only measured contrasts.

findings.issue: The sentence saying that the other 13 adjusted model-pair intervals include zero cites Table 2, which displays only the five comparisons against FLUX. The complete set of 15 comparisons is in Table 10.
findings.reader_effect: A reader attempting to verify the full inferential summary reaches a table that cannot show ten of the relevant comparisons.
findings.suggested_change: Cite Table 10 for the all-15 comparison statement, or cite Tables 2 and 10 together. This is a cross-reference replacement with no need to expand the manuscript.

summary: An excellent and self-contained account of a bounded digital-feature comparison. Its central distinction between detecting aligned painter responses and achieving low total mismatch is explained through concrete examples and informative figures, and the inferential limits are visible. Only localized abstract wording and cross-reference repairs are apparent; no consequential structural rewrite or new evidence is needed.
